scoring_justification: The agent produces aggregate simulation results (lifetimes, Arrhenius fits); recomputing the metric from raw MD trajectory files is infeasible in the verifier sandbox, so the checker compares the reported aggregates to paper-derived gold values with tolerances that absorb run-to-run spread.

schema.description: Two lines: 'O: ν = <value> THz ( <value> cm⁻¹ )' and 'U: ν = <value> THz ( <value> cm⁻¹ )'

outputs.description: Natural core-shell vibration frequencies for O and U, used to validate adiabatic separation.
Mean and standard deviation of recombination times for oxygen Frenkel pairs of ranks 3, 4I, 4II, 5 at temperatures 600, 900, 1200, 1500, 1800 K.
Arrhenius pre‑exponential factor and activation energy fitted from the recombination lifetimes for each oxygen Frenkel pair rank.

output_contract.notes: The task reproduces the core-shell vibration frequencies and the oxygen Frenkel pair recombination dynamics using the Meis-Chartier potential. Uranium Frenkel pairs, static formation energies, and isolated defect migration energies are excluded per the taskability scope, focusing on the main dynamic claim that polarizability alters oxygen FP recombination times.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold reference values for core-shell frequencies and oxygen FP recombination Arrhenius parameters.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table III (core-shell section) and the paper's reported Arrhenius fits for oxygen FP ranks 3, 4I, 4II, 5: τ = τ0 exp(Ea/kBT) with τ0 and Ea as given in the paper.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the paper's numerical claims in Eqs. (7)-(10) and Table III (core-shell column, this work).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact numbers the paper reports; they constitute the authoritative hidden gold. The reference solver writes the same values, so a correct reproduction must match them within tolerances.

steps.description: Compare O and U core-shell frequencies (THz and wavenumber) within 1% relative tolerance.

For each rank (3,4I,4II,5) and each temperature (600,900,1200,1500,1800 K), compare the reported mean lifetime to the gold value computed from the paper's Arrhenius fit; accept if relative error ≤ 20% or absolute error ≤ reported std.
Compare Ea_eV for each rank to gold (0.32, 0.11, 0.51, 0.57 eV) with tolerance ±0.05 eV, and verify monotonic ordering Ea(5) > Ea(4II) > Ea(3) > Ea(4I).
